Aero 1.2.1 is a quality-of-life release for 1.2. Requests that need doing get done, on screen, in your own signed-in browser. Tool calling is tuned for each model. Any model on Hugging Face loads at the size that fits your PC. Every integration comes installed.

## Install or update

Aero 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2.0 offer this update at startup (**Update now**). New installs:

| System | File | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Windows** 10 / 11 (64-bit) | `Aero-windows.zip` | Extract it, double-click `Update-Aero.bat`, accept the admin prompt. `--dest D:\Aero` installs elsewhere; `--lean` skips setting up the integrations now (Aero finishes them in the background). |
| **macOS** (Apple Silicon or Intel) | `Aero-macos.zip` | Unzip it, right-click `Install-Aero.command` → Open. |
| **Linux**, any distro | `install.sh` | `curl -fsSL https://github.com/NermalYT/Aero/releases/latest/download/install.sh \| sh` |
| Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Pop!_OS | `aero_1.2.1_all.deb` | `sudo apt install ./aero_1.2.1_all.deb` |
| Fedora, RHEL, Rocky, Alma, openSUSE | `aero-1.2.1-1.noarch.rpm` | `sudo dnf install ./aero-1.2.1-1.noarch.rpm` |
| Arch, Manjaro, EndeavourOS | `PKGBUILD` | `makepkg -si` |
| Any Linux, by hand | `Aero-linux.tar.gz` | `sh Aero/install.sh` |

Models, chats, memory, settings, keys, tunings, skills and mods carry over. After updating, Aero sets up the integrations you don't have yet in the background (about 14 GB in all), with a progress line under the workspaces.

## What's new

- **Ask for it and it gets done.** "Look at my GitHub notifications" or "check my emails and look for any meetings this week" is recognised before the model answers. Aero shows its plan, offers the right tools and works on screen. If a small model replies "I can't", Aero makes the first move with a grammar-forced tool call. Email means every account: the ones you list, mail sites in your bookmarks, Gmail (all signed-in accounts) and Outlook. Meetings come back as a table in the chat plus a Word schedule you can download.
- **Your own browser, already signed in.** Aero works in your default browser: Chrome, Edge, Brave or Vivaldi, not always Edge.
  - **To use the browser you're already signed in to:** switch on remote debugging at `chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging` (Chrome 144 or later). Settings → Tools copies the address for you.
  - **What happens then:** your browser asks you to Allow the connection. Aero opens its own tabs, never reads or closes yours, and lets go when it's done. Nothing is copied or decrypted.
  - **Without the switch:** Aero uses its own profile of your browser, and a sign-in page pauses with *I've signed in* / *Skip this site*. Aero never types a password.
- **No more tool-call text in the chat.** Calls a model writes as text are run instead of printed. That covers Hermes `<tool_call>`, Qwen3-Coder, GLM, Mistral, Llama, Granite, DeepSeek and Gemma. Steps that only call tools show just the tool cards.
- **Tool calling is part of tuning.** Every tune ends with an exam: 40 Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard cases plus 12 Aero requests. It picks the temperature for tool steps, and decides whether Aero should start actions for that model. Full tuning now keeps going until 8 trials in a row bring nothing better; on Qwen3-4B that took 22 trials, where 1.2.0 stopped at 8. The tuning advisor works again with this llama.cpp build.
- **Any model, any size.** Search all of Hugging Face. A repo with only the original weights lists the GGUF versions others made of it, or Aero makes one for your PC: llama.cpp's converter, an importance matrix for low-bit quants, then `llama-quantize`.
  - The tuner also tries splitting off only the feed-forward weights for dense models bigger than the GPU. Gemma-3-27B at Q8_0 ran 98k context in a 15 GB limit, where whole-layer offload ran out of memory at 131k.
  - Downloads are checked against Hugging Face's SHA-256.
- **Everything comes installed.** Hindsight, AirLLM, image generation, Flutter and the code tools are set up with Aero, not later.
- **Tidier.**
  - The Compact button is gone; compaction is automatic at 75%.
  - Text fields match the theme.
  - Workspace cards and the Big models panel open with arrows, and the Workspaces list folds away.
  - Files Aero makes get a Download button in the chat.

What was run on the test PC (Windows 11, RTX 5080): [V1.2_TOOL_CALLING.md](https://github.com/NermalYT/Aero/blob/main/source/docs/V1.2_TOOL_CALLING.md).
